issues.description: Neither ISS-0771 mutant (the outer rescue in TenantProvisioning.replay_all_pending/0, nor the outer rescue in MigrationReplayBoot.start_link/1) is caught by any current test, because replay_migrations/1's own internal rescue (tenant_provisioning.ex:395-397) already converts every raised exception from Ecto.Migrator.run/4 into a returned {:error, {:migration_failed, exception}} tuple before either outer rescue can ever be reached. Both outer rescues are real, deliberate defense-in-depth per the modules' own moduledocs ('two independent layers' / 'this function's exception-safety must not depend on replay_all_pending/0's own internal per-tenant rescue continuing to catch everything forever either') guarding against a future regression in that Layer-1 rescue, not against any presently reachable code path. Not a coverage gap actionable by TEST-DESIGNER: triggering Layer 2 would require injecting a bug that bypasses Layer 1's own rescue, which is not a realistic scenario to construct against a real (non-mocked) Postgres per this project's real-DB testing directive. Flagging for TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR/RELEASE-VALIDATOR to judge whether this redundancy is acceptable as-is or whether the design doc should be revisited.

Full suite has 2 pre-existing, reproducible-twice failures in test/letflow/identity_test.exs (REQ-019 AC1), caused by a documented cross-process race in test/support/bpm_default_realm_displacement.ex when a sibling mix test OS process is concurrently connected to the shared DB. Out of ISS-0771 scope (unrelated files, unrelated requirement, not touched by either mutant). Not something TEST-DESIGNER can fix without exceeding its role/owned_modules.
